comment: Hand-added river channels (rivers Task 11d fix round 1, the owner: 'Hand-add delta channels'): a delta's main channel where Natural Earth's course stops above it. Each entry is cited. Merged by `timefly-bake rivers-today` (tools/bake/timefly_bake/rivers_today.py) after Natural Earth's courses into rivers_today.json, which the pass burns; points [lat, lon], upstream first; `mouth` is the cited point each channel ends at.

rivers.name: Yangtze estuary
rivers.source: From the end of Natural Earth's Yangtze at Zhenjiang (32.197, 119.606) to the Yangtze's mouth on the East China Sea: Wikipedia, 'Yangtze' (read 2026-11-26), infobox mouth 31 23 37 N, 121 58 59 E. Course: the least-cost path over ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second cells (NOAA NCEI 2022, doi:10.25921/fd45-gt74) between the points named, a step costing its length x (1 + max(0, the cell's elevation in m)), so it keeps to the water; simplified to 1 km, points rounded to 0.001 degrees. It passes 12 km from Jiangyin's and 16 km from Nantong's article points (their city centres, off the banks).
rivers.note: Natural Earth's 1:10m Yangtze ends at Zhenjiang, about 300 km above the sea; without this the river left its course's end north across the Jiangsu lowland to the Yellow Sea (rivers Task 11d).

rivers.name: Hau (Bassac)
rivers.source: From the end of Natural Earth's Bassac arm at Can Tho (10.005, 105.838) to the Bassac's mouth on the South China Sea in Soc Trang province: Wikipedia, 'Bassac River' (read 2026-11-26), the article's coordinates 9 31 N, 106 13 E. Course: the least-cost path over ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second cells (NOAA NCEI 2022, doi:10.25921/fd45-gt74) between the points named, a step costing its length x (1 + max(0, the cell's elevation in m)), so it keeps to the water; simplified to 1 km, points rounded to 0.001 degrees.
rivers.note: Natural Earth's Bassac ends at Can Tho; without this the river turned west across the delta to the Gulf of Thailand (rivers Task 11d).

rivers.name: Tien
rivers.source: From the end of Natural Earth's Mekong (Tien) arm (10.238, 106.119) to the Mekong's mouth: Wikipedia, 'Mekong' (read 2026-11-26), infobox mouth 10.19 N, 106.75 E (the Mekong Delta); Wikipedia, 'Tien River' (read 2026-11-26), lists its distributaries, the Co Chien, Ham Luong, Ba Lai and My Tho. Course: the least-cost path over ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second cells (NOAA NCEI 2022, doi:10.25921/fd45-gt74) between the points named, a step costing its length x (1 + max(0, the cell's elevation in m)), so it keeps to the water; simplified to 1 km, points rounded to 0.001 degrees.
rivers.note: Natural Earth's Tien arm ends above the delta's mouths (rivers Task 11d).

rivers.name: Rio Grande (Orinoco)
rivers.source: The Orinoco's main distributary from the delta's head at Barrancas del Orinoco (Wikipedia, 'Barrancas del Orinoco', 8.70194 N, 62.19944 W) past Curiapo (Wikipedia, 'Curiapo', 8.58 N, 60.9975 W) to Barima Point (Wikipedia, 'Barima Point', 8.60722 N, 60.41083 W), all read 2026-11-26. Wikipedia, 'Orinoco Delta': 'The main distributary is called the Rio Grande, which empties south-southeast through the southern portion of the delta'. Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Orinoco River', places the delta's south-eastern end at Barima Point on the Boca Grande (the page refused an automated read; its text was read through a search engine's summary, 2026-11-26). Course: the least-cost path over ETOPO 2022 60 arc-second cells (NOAA NCEI 2022, doi:10.25921/fd45-gt74) between the points named, a step costing its length x (1 + max(0, the cell's elevation in m)), so it keeps to the water; simplified to 1 km, points rounded to 0.001 degrees.
rivers.note: Owner, 2026-11-26: 'Yes, add it'. Natural Earth's Orinoco reaches the sea by a northern distributary (rivers Task 11d).
